verses.text: You have really been helpful to someone weak and weary.
You have given great advice and wonderful wisdom to someone truly in need.
How can anyone possibly speak with such understanding?
Remember the terrible trembling of those in the world of the dead below the mighty ocean.
Nothing in that land of death and destruction is hidden from God,
who hung the northern sky and suspended the earth on empty space.
God stores water in clouds, but they don't burst,
and he wraps them around the face of the moon.
On the surface of the ocean, God has drawn a boundary line between light and darkness.
And columns supporting the sky tremble at his command.
By his power and wisdom, God conquered the force of the mighty ocean.

footnotes.text: the force of the mighty ocean: The Hebrew text has “the ocean … Rahab.” In this passage the sea monster Rahab stands for the fearsome power of the ocean (see the notes at 3.8 and 9.13).

verses.text: The heavens became bright when he breathed, and the escaping sea monster died at his hands.

footnotes.text: sea monster: The Hebrew text has “snake,” which probably stands for some kind of fearsome sea monster, such as Leviathan (see Isaiah 27.1).

verses.text: These things are merely a whisper of God's power at work. How little we would understand if this whisper ever turned into thunder!
